title: Bridges for kids
examples: Teacher, which bridge shape is the strongest?
Can we test which bridge holds the most toys?
What is the difference between a beam and an arch bridge?

explain.say: Today we will learn about different bridge shapes.
A beam bridge is like a straight plank across a gap.
An arch bridge uses curved stones to hold up the middle.
A suspension bridge hangs from strong cables across the gap.
We can test these bridges by carefully adding weights.

items: Add more weight until it breaks

draw.text: Testing: Add weights to find limit

explain.say: In real life, suspension bridges cross big rivers like the Golden Gate.

faq.q: Which bridge shape is the strongest one?
faq.a: It is hard to say just one is always the strongest. The best shape depends on the river and how much it needs to carry.
asks: Does arch bridge beat suspension bridge?
What is the best bridge design?

faq.q: Do all bridges have to be curved?
faq.a: No, some bridges, like simple beams, are straight. But curves help them be very strong.
asks: Can a straight bridge be strong enough?

faq.q: What do the cables do on a suspension bridge?
faq.a: The main cables carry the weight and hang the road deck below them. They spread the load out.
asks: Are the cables important for suspension bridges?

faq.q: How do we know if a bridge will break?
faq.a: We test it by adding weights slowly until it cannot hold any more. This shows its limit.
asks: How do we test bridge strength?

faq.q: Are beams only for short gaps?
faq.a: Beams work well for shorter gaps where the weight is spread evenly across the top.
asks: When should I use a beam bridge?

facts: Beams are straight structures that span a gap.
Arches use curved supports to transfer weight to the sides.
Suspension bridges use cables to hang the roadway.
Testing bridges involves adding weights to find their limit.

quiz.say: If you need a bridge for a very wide river, which shape is often used?
quiz.why: Suspension bridges are designed to span very long distances using cables.

wrong.0: Beams are usually best for shorter, straight gaps.
wrong.1: Arches are excellent but work best when the sides are solid.
wrong.2: All shapes can work, but suspension is famous for width.

quiz.say: Which shape uses curved supports to push weight outward?
quiz.why: The curve of the arch directs the weight sideways into the supports.

wrong.0: Beams only push straight down, which can cause them to bend.
wrong.1: Suspension relies on hanging cables, not curved pushing.
wrong.2: This is not a shape name, but a description.

quiz.say: If you build a bridge and it breaks when you add more weights, what did you find?
quiz.why: The point where it breaks tells you the most weight it could safely hold.

wrong.1: The color does not tell you how much weight it can hold.
wrong.2: Length is how far it goes, not how much it can carry.
wrong.3: The shape is what it is, not how much it can bear.
